newsitem.title: UK: MOTOR RACING-FORMER WORLD CHAMPION MANSELL OFFERED JORDAN DRIVE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-FORMER WORLD CHAMPION MANSELL OFFERED JORDAN DRIVE.

text.p: Former world champion Nigel Mansell, out of Formula One motor racing for more than a year, has been offered the chance of a grand prix comeback by the Jordan team.
But Jordan, based in Silverstone, said on Thursday the overture to the British driver had not been followed up.

Team boss Eddie Jordan contacted Mansell after Damon Hill, the new world champion, decided to join TWR Arrows. Mansell has been without a drive since he parted company with McLaren early in the 1995 season.
"Eddie did telephone Nigel to make inquiries when Damon went to TWR because Nigel had indicated he would consider a drive," a Jordan spokeswoman said.
"But it was just a chat. There has been no direct dialogue or any on-going discussions since then."
Mansell, 43, indicated recently that he would be prepared to return to Formula One if the right offer from the right team came along.
Jordan are keen to partner the raw talent of Ralf Schumacher, younger brother of twice world champion Michael, with an experienced driver.
"Eddie is going to investigate every avenue when it comes to our second driver," the spokeswoman said. "It is not as if we have got to make a decision by the end of November or something.
"Ralf was always going to do the bulk of winter testing to get used to the car and the team. We are looking for the best driver available."
Mansell, world champion in 1992, suffered an embarrassing comeback in 1995. The cockpit of the McLaren was too small, forcing him to miss the first two races.
He eventually competed in two races before quitting amid complaints about the car's driving qualities.
Since then he has concentrated on his golf business. He has said that if he did return to motor racing then IndyCars in America would be the more likely avenue.
